questions.question: Which class is used to write text files in Java?
explanations: FileReader is used to read files, not to write them.
Correct. FileWriter and PrintWriter are the main classes for writing text files in Java.
BufferedWriter is used to improve performance, but it is not the main way to write.
System.out prints to the console, not to files.

questions.question: How do you write a line of text to a file with PrintWriter?
explanations: writeLine() is not a PrintWriter method.
Correct. println() writes the text followed by a line break to the file.
addLine() does not exist in PrintWriter.
insert() is not a PrintWriter method.

questions.question: What does the second parameter `true` do when creating a FileWriter?
options: Opens the file in append mode (add to the end)
Creates the file in binary mode
explanations: The boolean parameter does not control read-only mode.
Correct. When true is passed, the FileWriter opens the file in append mode and adds content to the end without overwriting.
It has nothing to do with compression.
FileWriter always works with text, not in binary mode.

questions.question: How do you write formatted text to a file in a way similar to System.out.printf()?
options: pw.format("%s is %d years old", name, age)
explanations: Correct. PrintWriter has the printf() and format() methods that work the same as System.out.printf().
printFormatted() is not a PrintWriter method.
fprintf() is from C, not Java.
formattedWrite() does not exist in PrintWriter.

questions.question: Which exception can FileWriter throw when trying to write to a file?
explanations: FileNotFoundException is thrown by FileReader, not by FileWriter when writing.
Correct. FileWriter can throw IOException when an I/O error occurs during writing.
FileWriteException does not exist in the standard Java API.
AccessException does not exist in the standard Java API.
